description.text: Two jumbo cards numbered with a J suffix, released alongside the P promos from August 2001 to July 2002: the smallest numbered Japanese promo set. Timeless Celebi came with the September 2001 issue of CoroCoro Comic, out in August 2001, and Latias and Latios with the theatrical release of the film Guardian Gods of the City of Water: Latias and Latios. Later jumbo cards often carry just the black star PROMO symbol, and more recent ones the suffix of the promo set of their day with no number.

tell.text: A black star symbol at the right, and a "/J" number

description.text:
A jumbo card given with the September 2001 issue of CoroCoro Comic, published on 15 August 2001, as its bottom edge says; its top line calls it the special jumbo card of Celebi: A Timeless Encounter, the fourth Pokémon film, which had opened in Japan on 7 July 2001. Atsuko Nishida's Celebi, named Timeless Celebi, carries CoroCoro's logo in its corner. Its one attack lets each player put any number of Basic Pokémon from their discard pile onto their Bench.

It is the first of the two J promos, jumbo cards numbered as promos; the second, Latias and Latios 002/J, came the next year.

tell.text: An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.

description.text:
A jumbo card given out at cinemas showing Guardian Gods of the City of Water: Latias and Latios, the fifth Pokémon film, which opened in Japan on 13 July 2002 and came out in English as Pokémon Heroes. Its top line calls it a cinema-only jumbo card for the fifth anniversary of Pikachu the Movie, whose logo is printed at the bottom.

Latias and Latios fly past four circles holding Celebi, Mewtwo, Entei and Lugia, and no illustrator is credited. Its one attack lets you take any of the Pokémon in the circles from your own collection and put them onto your Bench, even when it is full. Its text says those four appear somewhere in the film in another form, gives a hint (look at the tiles of the secret garden's floor), and sends readers to the film's website for the answer. It is the second of the two J promos, jumbo cards numbered as promos, after Timeless Celebi 001/J.

tell.text: An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.
